overall.verdict: A genuinely honest and technically literate wallet whose green=vours/violet=promise discipline and signed-receipt evidence are best-in-class for self-custodial UX, but it buries that strength under dense educational paragraphs, unexplained jargon (capacity, frames, entity id, collateral tariffs) and an inconsistent two-color system that a third amber breaks. Most tasks are completable by a confident user; the 15% of users who most need safety (Rosa, Lucas, Aisha) are the ones the copy serves worst.
priority_fixes: Deduplicate the green/violet explainer into one dismissible, canonical lesson and enforce two colors everywhere (kill the amber book bars or label them)

Rewrite all capacity/collateral copy in outcome language: 'can send up to X', 'can receive up to Y', '$115 promised to you, $0 secured on-chain' — one canonical exposure sentence reused on Home, Account and Sovereignty
Make every credit/collateral action (Extend credit limit, 0% collateral slider) require an explicit 'permanent, unsecured' confirmation with a plain risk sentence
Fix mechanical defects: clipped Move-into-reserve button, stuck toast over the cross-network swap card, truncated address card on 02-pay, inconsistent proof-hash truncation
Add action affordances at the point of exposure: 'Request collateral / Reduce exposure' on the account screen, 'Secure more' on Sovereignty, and a risk note plus market rate on Lending
